subject: Post-call: model fit follow-up & quality regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: RetailCo Data Science <ds@retailco.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: model fit follow-up & quality regression concern

Hi Olivia — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Key goals you shared: improve product recommendation relevancy for seasonal promotions, reduce incorrect upsell suggestions, and maintain latency <150ms p95 for the recommender API.
- Workload: mixed short prompts (<=128 tokens) for ranking + some longer multi-turn assistant examples.
- Current pain: after the last model update on your side, you saw a measurable drop in click-through for promoted items (~6% delta) and a few clear failure cases in our shared eval set.

Suggested immediate actions (we discussed):
1) Share the prompt/eval sets (you uploaded a sample; thanks) — we ran preliminary diffs. Included a short eval report and prompt set here (attached).
2) Recommended model variants: 1) redwood-7b:quant-v2 (good cost/latency balance) 2) redwood-13b:fp16 (higher quality for complex context). See the attached eval summary for per-slice scores.
3) Pin the currently-working model version for your production route while we investigate the regression and produce a diff summary.
4) Canary a rollback if the diff confirms degradation for your top slices.

Next steps from our side: I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) and Monica (CS) to run a more detailed regression analysis against your eval set and propose a rollback/pin plan with timelines. On your side, could you confirm which routes need pinning and share any rate/traffic constraints for canarying?

Attachments: redwood-eval-report-v2.pdf, retailco-prompt-set.jsonl

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We confirmed the CTR drop correlates with a model version bump that our infra team rolled on Aug 24.
- Example failures attached inline below (copied from our QA): one-shot prompts giving irrelevant category predictions for seasonal SKUs; ranking order swapping high-margin items out of top 3.
- Routes to pin: /recommend/v2 and /upsell-slate. These are the ones with highest revenue impact.
- Canary constraints: we can take up to 10% traffic to a pinned older model initially, then 30% after 48 hours if stable.

Can you and your team confirm you can produce a diff report by tomorrow EOD and whether pinning the previous production model is an immediate option?

Best,

Thanks Marissa — I pulled the prompt set and ran a quick diff between the currently-deployed variant (redwood-7b:quant-v3 @ build 20260820) and the previous production variant (redwood-7b:quant-v2 @ build 20260710). High-level findings: 

- Overall micro-F1 on your annotated slice dropped 4.8 points on the newer build; biggest regressions on seasonal-category prompts and long-context ranking queries.
- Token-level latency is similar (p95 ~120ms) for both quant-v2 and quant-v3 on our test infra; so this looks like a model-quality delta not a perf tradeoff.
- I reproduced two of Olivia's examples: the newer build re-ranked a high-margin SKU lower due to a probability redistribution on the top-5 logits.

Recommendation: 
1) Pin redwood-7b:quant-v2 for /recommend/v2 and /upsell-slate immediately (we can flip routing config) and enable a 10% canary to the newer build for monitoring.
2) Produce a formal eval diff report (I’ll attach per-slice CSV and a short PDF). Tentative ETA: 8 hours for the full diff + recommended rollback plan.
3) If you want higher quality, propose testing redwood-13b:fp16 on a small test shard for the complex slices — expect higher tokens cost but improved correctness on long-context queries.

Operational notes: pinning is a config change on RetailCo's route mapping we can coordinate with their infra team; rollback permanently requires version pin in routing until they approve upgrade.

I’ll attach the quick diff in the follow-up email.

— Rishi
